target_customer: Crypto exchanges, financial institutions, and government investigators and regulators
problem: Crypto businesses and agencies need to trace illicit funds and screen wallets and transactions for compliance.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API subscription for compliance and investigations

founders.name: Esteban Castano
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and CEO by The Block (2021-06) and the YC page; background not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Rahul Raina
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on the YC page; role CTO from a profile site seen in search only.

competitors.name: Chainalysis
competitors.what: Crypto compliance and investigation software including the KYT product
competitors.traction_then: KYT served more than 100 financial institutions and exchanges; revenue tripled since April 2018
competitors.funding_then: $30M Series B led by Accel in February 2019, total about $48M

competitors.name: Elliptic
competitors.what: UK crypto analytics provider named as a competitor to Chainalysis

technical_complexity.rationale: Attribution and clustering across many blockchains with data engineering at scale is hard for a small team, though prior art by Chainalysis existed.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated attribution data and law enforcement relationships compound; yet two funded competitors already had a lead in 2019.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition occurred; TRM raised later rounds and by 2026 reports a $1 billion valuation.

market_need_then: Chainalysis raised $30M in February 2019 and reported more than 100 financial institution customers for transaction monitoring, showing compliance spend by exchanges.

branding.community_and_virality: Co-produced work with FRONTLINE and the AP on the documentary Scammed per the 2026 homepage.

identity.voice_and_tone: Urgent, confident and mission driven; crime fighters versus criminals framing

brand_strength.rationale: Recognised in crypto compliance and government circles with customers like Coinbase and Circle named, but acronym name and no mascot or consumer community.

pivots.to: AI investigation platform (Ardence) for law enforcement and national security
pivots.why: Company positioning on 2026 homepage and Series C release; the exact date not sourced.

outcome_analysis: TRM Labs entered YC in Summer 2019 against the funded leader Chainalysis and grew with regulatory demand for crypto compliance. It raised a 14 million dollar Series A in 2021, a 60 million dollar Series B later that year, a 70 million dollar extension from Thoma Bravo in 2022 and a 70 million dollar Series C at a 1 billion dollar valuation in February 2026. Revenue is reported to grow 150 percent a year, and it is one of the strongest outcomes in the batch.
notes: The 2019 $4.2M and earlier $1.7M amounts come from The Block's 2021 Series A article, which does not label them or list dates for the earlier one. The December 2021 $60M Series B led by Tiger Global was seen via SiliconANGLE (date) and a Blockworks result in search; the Nov 2022 $70M is labeled a Series B extension by the search summary of The Block; no post-money stated for 2021 and 2022 rounds. Some outlets attach the $1B valuation to the 2022 round, but The Block says the company declined to disclose it then. Fintech News and Fortune report a later extension at a $2B valuation (amount undisclosed), not recorded as a round. Fortune dates the Series C to September; most outlets say 4 February 2026. Founders' prior employers and education not found in opened sources. Name expansion was not found.
